AC.L2-3.1.10a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines the period of inactivity and when a session lock is defined.
AC.L2-3.1.10a.assessment_considerations: If session locks are not managed centrally, how are all computer users made aware of the requirements and how to configure them?

AC.L2-3.1.10b.evidence_examples: Artifact that shows the setting of session lock (GPO or system policy or similar solution addressing the controls supporting centralized management and configuration of operating systems, applications, and users' settings for the working environment of user accounts and computer accounts).
AC.L2-3.1.10b.assessment_considerations: If session locks are not managed centrally, how are all computer users made aware of the requirements and how to configure them?

AC.L2-3.1.10c.evidence_examples: Screenshot of GPO setting and configuration settings, or similar solution addressing the controls supporting centralized management and configuration of operating systems, applications, and users' settings for the working environment of user accounts and computer accounts.
AC.L2-3.1.10c.assessment_considerations: [i] If session locks are not managed centrally, how are all computer users made aware of the requirements and how to configure them? [ii] Does the session lock hide previously visible information (e.g., replacing what was visible with a lock screen or screensaver that does not include sensitive information)?

AC.L2-3.1.11a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines the conditions requiring a user session to be terminated.
AC.L2-3.1.11a.assessment_considerations: [i] Are the conditions in which a user session must be terminated described (e.g., after a period of inactivity or after a defined time limit)? [ii] Are user sessions terminated based on organizationally defined conditions?

AC.L2-3.1.11b.evidence_examples: Screen share showing GPO / VPN Settings that show when a session would be terminated (Idle time, max connection time).
AC.L2-3.1.11b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are procedures documented that describe how to configure the system to enable automatic termination of user sessions after any of the defined conditions occur? [ii] Are user sessions terminated based on organizationally defined conditions?

AC.L2-3.1.12a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines remote access sessions.
AC.L2-3.1.12a.assessment_considerations: Do policies identify when remote access is permitted and what methods must be used?

AC.L2-3.1.12b.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines remote access is permitted.
AC.L2-3.1.12b.assessment_considerations: Do policies identify when remote access is permitted and what methods must be used?

AC.L2-3.1.12c.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows how the remote access is controlled (access session, and or groups).
AC.L2-3.1.12c.assessment_considerations: Are systems configured to permit only approved remote access sessions (e.g., disallow remote access sessions by default)?

AC.L2-3.1.12d.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows how remote sessions are monitored (logs).
AC.L2-3.1.12d.assessment_considerations: Are automated or manual mechanisms employed for monitoring remote connections? If the monitoring is manual, does it occur at a frequency commensurate with the level of risk?

AC.L2-3.1.13a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that discusses the CUI rules, consistent, and associated with the specific CUI category; FIPS Cert # of appliance or application.
AC.L2-3.1.13a.assessment_considerations: Are cryptographic mechanisms used for remote access sessions (e.g., Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) using FIPS-validated encryption algorithms) defined and implemented? Note that simply using an approved algorithm is not sufficient – the module (software and/or hardware) used to implement the algorithm must be separately validated under FIPS 140.

AC.L2-3.1.13b.evidence_examples: Screenshot of VPN concentration that shows encryption is on and enabled (point-to-point, etc.).
AC.L2-3.1.13b.assessment_considerations: Are cryptographic mechanisms used for remote access sessions (e.g., Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) using FIPS-validated encryption algorithms) defined and implemented? Note that simply using an approved algorithm is not sufficient – the module (software and/or hardware) used to implement the algorithm must be separately validated under FIPS 140.

AC.L2-3.1.14a.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows access control points (groups and/or users).
AC.L2-3.1.14a.assessment_considerations: How many managed access control points are implemented?

AC.L2-3.1.14b.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows access control points and how they are managed.
AC.L2-3.1.14b.assessment_considerations: Is all remote access routed through the managed access control points?

AC.L2-3.1.15a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines what is authorized to be executed remotely and how that is handled.
AC.L2-3.1.15a.assessment_considerations: Does system documentation identify system administration or security functions that can be executed remotely?

AC.L2-3.1.15b.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines what can be accessed remotely and what procedures are implemented to allow this (RDP, jump box).

AC.L2-3.1.15c.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows who has access to perform privileged commands a remotely (access groups for privileged accounts).
AC.L2-3.1.15c.assessment_considerations: Is execution of the identified privileged commands via remote access only authorized for documented operational needs?

AC.L2-3.1.15d.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows the routing of remote access and how it is monitored and how many locations (Firewall, VPN Concentrator).

AC.L2-3.1.16a.assessment_considerations: Is an updated list of approved network devices providing wireless access to the system maintained?

AC.L2-3.1.16b.evidence_examples: Authorization profile(s) in Wireless Access Controller or Identity Manager (i.e. Cisco ISE).
AC.L2-3.1.16b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are network devices providing wireless access configured to require users or devices be authorized prior to permitting a wireless connection? [ii] Is wireless access to the system authorized and managed?

AC.L2-3.1.17a.evidence_examples: Security page (or similar) of a Wireless Access Controller.
AC.L2-3.1.17a.assessment_considerations: [i] Is wireless access limited only to authenticated and authorized users (e.g., required to supply a username and password)? [ii] If the organization is securing its wireless network with a pre-shared key, is access to that key restricted to only authorized users?

AC.L2-3.1.17b.evidence_examples: Security page (or similar) of a Wireless Access Controller.
AC.L2-3.1.17b.assessment_considerations: Is wireless access encrypted using FIPS-validated cryptography? Note that simply using an approved algorithm is not sufficient; the module (software and/or hardware) used to implement the algorithm must be separately validated under FIPS 140.

AC.L2-3.1.18a.assessment_considerations: Is a list of mobile devices that are permitted to process, store, or transmit CUI maintained?

AC.L2-3.1.18b.evidence_examples: Authorization profile(s) in Wireless Access Controller or Identity Manager (i.e. Cisco ISE)
AC.L2-3.1.18b.assessment_considerations: [i] Is a list of mobile devices that are permitted to process, store, or transmit CUI maintained? [ii] Is the system configured to only permit connections from identified, authorized mobile devices?

AC.L2-3.1.18c.evidence_examples: Mobile device logs within the MDM, log intake (sources) configuration (within SIEM) showing MDM is feeding logs to the SIEM.

AC.L2-3.1.19a.assessment_considerations: Is a list maintained of mobile devices and mobile computing platforms that are permitted to process, store, or transmit CUI?

AC.L2-3.1.19b.evidence_examples: Security policy page in MDM showing how encryption are enforced on mobile device. If no MDM or MDM doesn't enforce encryption, then validate if the devices used are on the list of devices with native FIPS approved validation.
AC.L2-3.1.19b.assessment_considerations: Is CUI encrypted on mobile devices using FIPS-validated algorithms?

AC.L2-3.1.1a.evidence_examples: Document defining account request, approval, provisioning.
AC.L2-3.1.1a.assessment_considerations: Is a list of authorized users maintained that defines their identities and roles?

AC.L2-3.1.1b.evidence_examples: Document defining account request, approval, provisioning.

AC.L2-3.1.1c.evidence_examples: Document defining account request, approval, provisioning.

AC.L2-3.1.1d.evidence_examples: Screen share showing login requirements are enforced. Example of an unauthorized user denied (unauthorized username entered at login).
AC.L2-3.1.1d.assessment_considerations: Are account requests authorized before system access is granted?

AC.L2-3.1.1e.evidence_examples: Screenshot showing that service accounts are assigned to authorized users only; no rogue accounts without an authorized user are active.
AC.L2-3.1.1e.assessment_considerations: Are account requests authorized before system access is granted?

AC.L2-3.1.1f.evidence_examples: Screen share showing that all devices running are authorized; no rogue devices on the network.
AC.L2-3.1.1f.assessment_considerations: Are account requests authorized before system access is granted?

AC.L2-3.1.20a.assessment_considerations: Are all connections to external systems outside of the assessment scope identified?

AC.L2-3.1.20b.assessment_considerations: Are external systems (e.g., systems managed by contractors, partners, or vendors; personal devices) that are permitted to connect to or make use of organizational systems identified?

AC.L2-3.1.20c.evidence_examples: SLA for external systems, memorandum for interconnection, information to prove that any cloud solution is at FedRAMP impact level of moderate or higher (i.e. license information, screenshot of AWS cloud dashboard, purchase order document).
AC.L2-3.1.20c.assessment_considerations: Are methods employed to ensure that only authorized connections are being made to external systems (e.g., requiring log-ins or certificates, access from a specific IP address, or access via Virtual Private Network (VPN))?

AC.L2-3.1.20d.evidence_examples: SLA for external systems, memorandum for interconnection, information to prove that any cloud solution is at FedRAMP impact level of moderate or higher (i.e. license information, screenshot of AWS cloud dashboard, Ppurchase order document).
AC.L2-3.1.20d.assessment_considerations: Are methods employed to confirm that only authorized external systems are connecting (e.g., if employees are receiving company email on personal cell phones, is the contractor checking to verify that only known/expected devices are connecting)?

AC.L2-3.1.20e.evidence_examples: Firewall ruleset for controlling access to cloud service or external system.
AC.L2-3.1.20e.assessment_considerations: Are methods employed to ensure that only authorized connections are being made to external systems (e.g., requiring log-ins or certificates, access from a specific IP address, or access via Virtual Private Network (VPN))?

AC.L2-3.1.20f.evidence_examples: Firewall ruleset for controlling access to cloud service or external system.
AC.L2-3.1.20f.assessment_considerations: Is the use of external systems limited, including by policy or physical control?

AC.L2-3.1.21a.evidence_examples: SSP, Removable Media Policy, Acceptable Use Policy (with emphasis on portable media use).
AC.L2-3.1.21a.assessment_considerations: Are the portable storage devices authorized for external use identified and documented?

AC.L2-3.1.21b.evidence_examples: SSP, Removable Media Policy, Acceptable Use Policy (with emphasis on portable media use).
AC.L2-3.1.21b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are the circumstances defined in which portable storage devices containing CUI may be used on external systems (e.g., with management approval)? [ii] Are limitations stipulated for the use of portable storage devices containing CUI on external systems (e.g., authorized personnel only, encrypted drives required)?

AC.L2-3.1.21c.evidence_examples: SSP, Removable Media Policy, Acceptable Use Policy (with emphasis on portable media use).

AC.L2-3.1.22b.evidence_examples: SSP, Website Governance Plan, Information Release Document.

AC.L2-3.1.22c.evidence_examples: Information release approval process, i.e. chain of email communication from originator, approver, and final decision (may or may not include individual authorized to post); SharePoint/electronic or paper form/ ticket system showing information flow between requestor and approver (may or may not include individual authorized to post).
AC.L2-3.1.22c.assessment_considerations: Does information on externally facing systems (i.e., publicly accessible) have a documented approval chain for public release ?

AC.L2-3.1.22d.evidence_examples: Incident response process, web design/update/modification SOP etc.

AC.L2-3.1.22e.evidence_examples: Incident response process, web design/update/modification SOP etc.

AC.L2-3.1.2a.evidence_examples: SSP, AUP, or IAM document that defines what authorized users can execute.
AC.L2-3.1.2a.assessment_considerations: Are access control lists used to limit access to applications and data based on role and/or identity?

AC.L2-3.1.2b.evidence_examples: Screenshot of security roles in AD or IAM or other directory-based identity-related services tool that shows transactions are as defined in the SSP or IAM document; privileged and non-privileged accounts need to be defined and identified in the artifact; screenshot of a non-privileged user trying to execute a privileged function.
AC.L2-3.1.2b.assessment_considerations: Is access for authorized users restricted to those parts of the system they are explicitly permitted to use (e.g., a person who only performs word-processing cannot access developer tools)?

AC.L2-3.1.3a.evidence_examples: SSP or other document describing the control of CUI on the network.

AC.L2-3.1.3b.evidence_examples: Document that defines the networking devices that are on the CUI network and answers what measures are in place to control the flow. List of firewalls, border and internal layer 3 devices, IDS/IPS, DLP, that process CUI.

AC.L2-3.1.3c.evidence_examples: Network diagram, data flow diagram, external system connection diagrams, document describing the policies for CUI on the network; listing of VLANs and subnets where CUI is authorized; document must describe source and authorized destinations.
AC.L2-3.1.3c.assessment_considerations: [i] Are designated sources of regulated data identified within the system (e.g., internal network and IP address) and between interconnected systems (e.g., external networks, IP addresses, ports, and protocols)? [ii] Are designated destinations of regulated data identified within the system (e.g., internal network and IP address) and between interconnected systems (external networks and IP addresses)?

AC.L2-3.1.3d.evidence_examples: Document that defines how CUI is to be controlled, such as an InfoSec plan, and/or network management plan.
AC.L2-3.1.3d.assessment_considerations: Are authorizations defined for each source and destination within the system and between interconnected systems (e.g., allow or deny rules for each combination of source and destination)?

AC.L2-3.1.3e.evidence_examples: Screenshots of firewall rules, ACLs, etc.
AC.L2-3.1.3e.assessment_considerations: Are approved authorizations for controlling the flow of regulated data enforced within the system and between interconnected systems (e.g., traffic between authorized sources and destinations is allowed and traffic between unauthorized sources and destinations is denied)?

AC.L2-3.1.4a.evidence_examples: Document, SSP, account management policy, defining separation of duties by person or role.
AC.L2-3.1.4a.assessment_considerations: Does system documentation identify the system functions or processes that require separation of duties (e.g., function combinations that represent a conflict of interest or an over-allocation of security privilege for one individual)?

AC.L2-3.1.4b.evidence_examples: Screenshot showing that separation of duties is enforced by showing admin accounts are assigned to different people based on role.

AC.L2-3.1.4c.evidence_examples: Screen shot showing an example such as a security manager can not log into a network device and change ACLs, or network admins can not access security logs in the SIEM tool.

AC.L2-3.1.5a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) identify what is considered a privileged account.
AC.L2-3.1.5a.assessment_considerations: Are privileged accounts documented and is when they may be used defined?

AC.L2-3.1.5b.evidence_examples: An artifact that identifies the least amount of permissions associated with different types of privileged accounts are approved.
AC.L2-3.1.5b.assessment_considerations: Are users assigned privileged accounts to perform their job functions only when it is necessary?

AC.L2-3.1.5c.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) identifies what is considered a security account.
AC.L2-3.1.5c.assessment_considerations: Are necessary security functions identified (e.g., access control configuration, system configuration settings, or privileged account lists) that must be managed through the use of privileged accounts?

AC.L2-3.1.5d.evidence_examples: Artifact(s) that identify the least amount of permissions associated with different types of security accounts are approved.
AC.L2-3.1.5d.assessment_considerations: Is access to privileged functions and security information restricted to authorized employees?

AC.L2-3.1.6a.evidence_examples: SSP or account management document, AUP, that defines non-security functions.
AC.L2-3.1.6a.assessment_considerations: Are nonsecurity functions and non-privileged roles defined?

AC.L2-3.1.6b.evidence_examples: Screenshot showing that a privileged user tried to use their admin account to access a non-security function, such as a browser or email (whatever is defined in their policy) and was blocked.
AC.L2-3.1.6b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are nonsecurity functions and non-privileged roles defined? [ii] Is it required that nonsecurity functions only be accessed with the use of non-privileged accounts? How is this verified?

AC.L2-3.1.7a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines privileged functions.
AC.L2-3.1.7a.assessment_considerations: Are the privileged system functions documented (e.g., functions that involve the control, monitoring or administration of the system, including security functions and log management)?

AC.L2-3.1.7b.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) that defines non-privileged users.

AC.L2-3.1.7c.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows that a non-privileged user is not allowed to complete a privileged function (installing software).
AC.L2-3.1.7c.assessment_considerations: Do documented procedures describe the configuration of the system to ensure system roles do not grant non-privileged users the ability to execute privileged functions?

AC.L2-3.1.7d.evidence_examples: Screen share that shows logs being captured of the execution of privileged functions.
AC.L2-3.1.7d.assessment_considerations: [i] Is it possible to identify who enabled privileges at any particular time? [ii] Do procedures describe the configuration of system settings to capture the execution of all privileged functions in audit logs?

AC.L2-3.1.8a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) showing unsuccessful logon attempts settings and or policy.
AC.L2-3.1.8a.assessment_considerations: Is there a defined threshold for the number of unsuccessful logon attempts for which the system takes action to prevent additional attempts?

AC.L2-3.1.8b.evidence_examples: Artifact showing GPO / Policy for limiting logon attempts.
AC.L2-3.1.8b.assessment_considerations: Is a mechanism for limiting the number of unsuccessful logon attempts implemented and does it use the defined threshold?

AC.L2-3.1.9a.evidence_examples: SSP or policy (documentation) showing CUI-specified rules are identified, consistent, and associated with the specific CUI category.
AC.L2-3.1.9a.assessment_considerations: [i] Are requirements identified for privacy and security notices, and do the implemented practices match those identified requirements? Discrepancies may indicate a deficient process and/or an incomplete practice. [ii] Are there any special requirements associated with the specific CUI category?

AC.L2-3.1.9b.evidence_examples: Artifact that shows a consent banner or screen that a user sees as they log in to the system.
AC.L2-3.1.9b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are requirements identified for privacy and security notices, and do the implemented practices match those identified requirements? Discrepancies may indicate a deficient process and/or an incomplete practice. [ii] Are appropriate notices displayed in areas where paper-based CUI is stored and processed?

PE.L2-3.10.1a.assessment_considerations: Are lists of personnel with authorized access developed and maintained, and are appropriate authorization credentials issued?

PE.L2-3.10.1b.evidence_examples: Badge reader logs, audit logs, and/or card swipe test.
PE.L2-3.10.1b.assessment_considerations: Has the facility/building manager designated building areas as “sensitive” and designed physical security protections (e.g., guards, locks, cameras, card readers) to limit physical access to the area to only authorized employees?

PE.L2-3.10.1c.evidence_examples: Badge reader logs, audit logs, and/or card swipe test.
PE.L2-3.10.1c.assessment_considerations: [i] Are output devices such as printers placed in areas where their use does not expose data to unauthorized individuals? [ii] Has the facility/building manager designated building areas as “sensitive” and designed physical security protections (e.g., guards, locks, cameras, card readers) to limit physical access to the area to only authorized employees?

PE.L2-3.10.1d.evidence_examples: Badge reader logs, audit logs, and/or card swipe test.
PE.L2-3.10.1d.assessment_considerations: Has the facility/building manager designated building areas as “sensitive” and designed physical security protections (e.g., guards, locks, cameras, card readers) to limit physical access to the area to only authorized employees?

PE.L2-3.10.2a.evidence_examples: Physical security measures and barriers into the physical facility (cameras/locks/gates/guards, etc.).

PE.L2-3.10.2b.evidence_examples: Physical barriers to entries into computer spaces, server rooms, etc..

PE.L2-3.10.2c.evidence_examples: Audit logs/how the physical facility is being monitored (cameras/access system/guards, etc.).
PE.L2-3.10.2c.assessment_considerations: Is physical access monitored to detect and respond to physical security incidents?

PE.L2-3.10.2d.evidence_examples: Audit logs/how the physical facility is being monitored (cameras/access system/guards, etc.).
PE.L2-3.10.2d.assessment_considerations: Is physical access monitored to detect and respond to physical security incidents?

PE.L2-3.10.3a.evidence_examples: Policy/procedures/instruction on methodology for handling non-authorized personnel (entry to exit).
PE.L2-3.10.3a.assessment_considerations: Are personnel required to accompany visitors to areas in a facility with physical access to organizational systems?

PE.L2-3.10.3b.evidence_examples: Policy/procedures/instructio on methodology for handling non-authorized personnel (entry to exit).
PE.L2-3.10.3b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are visitors clearly distinguishable from regular personnel? [ii] Is visitor activity monitored (e.g., use of cameras or guards, reviews of secure areas upon visitor departure, review of visitor audit logs)?

PE.L2-3.10.4a.evidence_examples: Log or report from badging system.
PE.L2-3.10.4a.assessment_considerations: [i] Are logs of physical access to sensitive areas (both authorized access and visitor access) maintained per retention requirements? [ii] Are visitor access records retained for as long as required?

PE.L2-3.10.5a.evidence_examples: Physical access control systems description, guard force contract/policy, key locks, logical systems specifications, etc..
PE.L2-3.10.5a.assessment_considerations: Are lists or inventories of physical access devices maintained (e.g., keys, facility badges, key cards)?

PE.L2-3.10.5b.evidence_examples: Inventory records of physical access control devices (e.g. keys, locks, card readers, locks, etc.).
PE.L2-3.10.5b.assessment_considerations: Is access to physical access devices limited (e.g., granted to, and accessible only by, authorized individuals)?

PE.L2-3.10.5c.evidence_examples: List of security safeguards controlling access to the facility (e.g. cameras, monitoring by guards, isolation of IT systems equiment and or system components).
PE.L2-3.10.5c.assessment_considerations: Are physical access devices managed (e.g., revoking key card access when necessary, changing locks as needed, maintaining access control devices and systems)?

PE.L2-3.10.6a.evidence_examples: Telework agreement, Acceptable Use Policy and SOP for alternate work locations; user security training validation which includes physical/logical/technical protections of system at alternate work sites.

PE.L2-3.10.6b.evidence_examples: Monitoring/audit log of user activity and logical/physical/technical mechanisms in place to preclude unauthorized activity (telework agrement , AUP?).
PE.L2-3.10.6b.assessment_considerations: [i] Do all alternate sites where CUI data is stored or processed meet the same physical security requirements as the main site? [ii] Does the alternate processing site provide information security measures equivalent to those of the primary site?

RA.L2-3.11.1b.evidence_examples: Copy of last risk assessment done within defined frequency.
RA.L2-3.11.1b.assessment_considerations: [i] Have initial and periodic risk assessments been conducted? [ii] Are methods defined for assessing risk (e.g., reviewing security assessments, incident reports, and security advisories, identifying threat sources, threat events, and vulnerabilities, and determining likelihood, impact, and overall risk to the confidentiality of CUI)?

RA.L2-3.11.2a.assessment_considerations: [i] Is the frequency specified for vulnerability scans to be performed in organizational systems and applications (e.g., continuous passive scanning, scheduled active scans)? [ii] Are vulnerability scans performed on a defined frequency or randomly in accordance with company policy?

RA.L2-3.11.2b.evidence_examples: System configuration settings of vulnerability scanning scheduling and vulnerability scan results of systems within defined frequency.
RA.L2-3.11.2b.assessment_considerations: Are vulnerability scans performed on a defined frequency or randomly in accordance with company policy?

RA.L2-3.11.2c.evidence_examples: System configuration settings of vulnerability scanning scheduling and vulnerability scan results of applications within defined frequency.
RA.L2-3.11.2c.assessment_considerations: Are vulnerability scans performed on a defined frequency or randomly in accordance with company policy?

RA.L2-3.11.2d.evidence_examples: View signatures in scanning tool/ad hoc scan performed as a result.
RA.L2-3.11.2d.assessment_considerations: [i] Are systems periodically scanned for common and new vulnerabilities? [ii] Is the list of scanned system vulnerabilities updated on a defined frequency or when new vulnerabilities are identified and reported?

RA.L2-3.11.2e.evidence_examples: View signatures in scanning tool/ad hoc scan performed as a result.
RA.L2-3.11.2e.assessment_considerations: [i] Are systems periodically scanned for common and new vulnerabilities? [ii] Is the list of scanned system vulnerabilities updated on a defined frequency or when new vulnerabilities are identified and reported?

RA.L2-3.11.3b.evidence_examples: Screenshot/document of scan results of remediated vulnerabilities in accordance to risk assessments.
RA.L2-3.11.3b.assessment_considerations: [i] Are the results of risk assessments used to prioritize vulnerabilities for remediation? [ii] For any given vulnerability is action taken for remediation, acceptance, avoidance, or transference of the vulnerability risk? [iii] Are all high risk vulnerabilities prioritized?

CA.L2-3.12.1a.assessment_considerations: Are security controls assessed at least annually?

CA.L2-3.12.1b.evidence_examples: Copy of last security control assessment done within defined frequency.
CA.L2-3.12.1b.assessment_considerations: Is the output of the security controls assessment documented?

CA.L2-3.12.2a.assessment_considerations: Is there an action plan to remediate identified weaknesses or deficiencies?

CA.L2-3.12.2b.assessment_considerations: Is the action plan maintained as remediation is performed?

CA.L2-3.12.2c.assessment_considerations: Does the action plan designate remediation dates and milestones for each item?

CA.L2-3.12.3a.evidence_examples: Collection of risk assessment results, internal or third-party audits/security assessments and/or continous monitoring reports/alerts (SIEM tool, etc.).
CA.L2-3.12.3a.assessment_considerations: [i] Are the security controls that need to be continuously monitored identified? [ii] Is the timeframe for continuous monitoring activities to support risk-based decision making defined? [iii] Is the output of continuous monitoring activities provided to stakeholders?

CA.L2-3.12.4a.assessment_considerations: Do mechanisms exist to develop and periodically update an SSP?

CA.L2-3.12.4d.evidence_examples: SSP and required adjudication from DoD CIO.
CA.L2-3.12.4d.assessment_considerations: Are security requirements identified and approved by the designated authority as non-applicable documented?

CA.L2-3.12.4g.assessment_considerations: Do mechanisms exist to develop and periodically update an SSP?

SC.L2-3.13.10a.evidence_examples: SSP, PKI/certificate management policy, configuration management.
SC.L2-3.13.10a.assessment_considerations: Are cryptographic keys established whenever cryptography is employed (e.g., digital signatures, authentication, authorization, transport, or other cryptographic mechanisms)?

SC.L2-3.13.10b.evidence_examples: SSP, PKI/certificate management policy, configuration management, access control policy.
SC.L2-3.13.10b.assessment_considerations: Are cryptographic keys maintained whenever cryptography is employed (e.g., key storage, backup, recovery, revocation, destruction, etc.)?

SC.L2-3.13.11a.assessment_considerations: Is cryptography implemented to protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest and in transit, through the configuration of systems and applications or through the use of encryption tools?
